body:
You have a point there, it would be good to get rid of this.

However, the opposing constraint is that when there is no custom Hashing object, some objects produce poor hashcodes for typical object ranges - for example (n: Int).hashCode == n.
The problem with this is that the upper bits of the hash code are usually always 0. In both concurrent and immutable tries this can cause a slowdown due to several collision levels. In parallel hash tables it causes a similar problem with parallel hash table construction.

So, ideally, we want to mangle the bits when a default is provided, and otherwise not mangle them and hope the user knows what he's doing.

Not being bound by the collections, I'd rather this had the signature

```
final def contains[A1 >: A](elem: A): Boolean
```

The difference is invisible at the user level but significant internally.  With an Any parameter it won't infer anything; with a bounded type parameter it will infer a type, the actual type of the parameter, which can then be checked.

Also, I don't think it particularly benefits from inlining.
